video_title: Shams Charania's insight on Jeanie Buss & siblings, Mark Walter + the Lakers | The Pat McAfee Show

quotes.speaker: Shams Charania
quotes.summary_phrase: Five of six Buss siblings voted to sell remaining Lakers stake
quotes.excerpt: Five of the six Buss siblings voted in favor of selling the remaining 17.8% final shares

text_blocks.speaker: Pat McAfee
text_blocks.text: Shams, did I get that right in my reporting of the reporting? And if I got any of that wrong, can you please correct me?

text_blocks.speaker: Shams Charania
text_blocks.text: You stated it all right. So that's what we know right now. Five of the six Buss siblings voted in favor of selling the remaining 17.8% final shares with the Los Angeles Lakers, along with Mark Walter. There is a tag-along provision that if Mark Walter ever sold, they could then as siblings, as part of their Buss family trust, have the majority votes to then sell along with Mark Walter.

quotes.speaker: Shams Charania
quotes.summary_phrase: Buss siblings invoke tag-along provision to sell Lakers stake
quotes.excerpt: They invoked the tag-along provision, so that's a sale of 17.8% at about 2.27 billion dollars.

text_blocks.speaker: Pat McAfee
text_blocks.text: I don't think anyone saw it coming that Mark Walter, less than 10 months after buying and officially transacting and closing on that sale of 10 billion dollars last year, would then sell and flip for 12.5 billion dollars.

text_blocks.speaker: Shams Charania
text_blocks.text: They invoked the tag-along provision, so that's a sale of 17.8% at about 2.27 billion dollars. And so they believe they have the majority votes to do so. Five of the six Buss siblings voted to sell. Jeanie's legal team put out a letter and her lawyer's interpretation is that she is the final voice, she is the only voice, and she is clearly willing to bring her lawyers in.

quotes.speaker: Shams Charania
quotes.summary_phrase: Jeanie Buss's legal team disputes validity of siblings' vote
quotes.excerpt: I had a statement from the Buss family trust. The first line of the statement from the lawyers said that I reported the six Buss siblings voted to sell. That key sentence right there is inaccurate.

text_blocks.speaker: Pat McAfee
text_blocks.text: Can you tell us a little bit if I got that right or wrong and where we sit on this beautiful Tuesday?

text_blocks.speaker: Shams Charania
text_blocks.text: I had a statement from the Buss family trust. The first line of the statement from the lawyers said that I reported the six Buss siblings voted to sell. That key sentence right there is inaccurate. And so I fully stand by my reporting. I've handled every story with care, including stories with the Lakers, as that statement continues on.

quotes.speaker: Shams Charania
quotes.summary_phrase: Josh Kushner and Bob Iger set to become majority Lakers owners
quotes.excerpt: Josh Kushner and Bob Iger are coming in now as the majority owners.

text_blocks.speaker: Pat McAfee
text_blocks.text: How are they handling it? Is Jeanie Buss still the controlling governor at about 17% when they bought in at 65%?

text_blocks.speaker: Shams Charania
text_blocks.text: Josh Kushner and Bob Iger are coming in now as the majority owners. Josh Kushner in my understanding was set up to be the controlling owner upon entrance of this, with Bob Iger handling a lot of the leadership and the day-to-day operations at the ownership position. And so if that's the case, how are you, and Bob Iger went on the record saying that they have a lot of respect for Jeanie Buss and they intend to honor the word of Mark Walter and Jeanie Buss, but if things changed, they'll change.

quotes.speaker: Shams Charania
quotes.summary_phrase: Lakers VP of Finance attempted to freeze shares before sale
quotes.excerpt: A Lakers VP of Finance actually called for a meeting to create a new trust to basically lock down and freeze everyone's shares through the next four years.

text_blocks.speaker: Pat McAfee
text_blocks.text: Is there a practice facility that they own?

text_blocks.speaker: Shams Charania
text_blocks.text: Last Tuesday, a Lakers VP of Finance actually called for a meeting to create a new trust to basically lock down and freeze everyone's shares through the next four years, which would line up with the remainder of Jeanie Buss's governorship. And the family did not agree to it to my understanding. They were caught off guard like, why is the VP of Finance on a random Tuesday trying to lock in all of the shares of the team to a new trust?
